channelTitle: A jar quietly fermenting on the counter did more for Grandma June's stomach than any pill
hook: A jar of cabbage quietly fermenting on the counter did more for Grandma June's stomach than any pill.
remedy: As a classic piece of old-fashioned home wisdom, cabbage packed in salt and left to ferment for a few weeks turns tangy and alive with natural cultures, and a small glass of the brine before a meal was an old way to settle the stomach and help digestion.
steps: Shred a head of cabbage and mix it with salt until it releases its own juice
Pack it tightly into a clean jar so the liquid covers the cabbage completely
Cover loosely and let it ferment at room temperature for two to four weeks, then refrigerate and sip a small glass of the brine before meals
caution: High in vitamin K, so check with a doctor first if you take blood thinners like warfarin. Also skip it if you're on a low-sodium diet, and if the jar ever smells off or grows mold, throw the whole batch out.
cta: Have you ever fermented your own sauerkraut, or does this sound like too much waiting for you? Tell Grandma June in the comments.
